1.translation: Śrīdhara says that Hari Himself praises karma-yoga to reveal the meaning of the distinction between “That” and “Thou.” The means of karma-yoga and the means of knowledge-yoga were stated in the preceding two chapters as means to liberation; now He will elaborate karma-yoga through qualities such as offering action to Brahman and through discrimination of the meaning of “thou.” First, praising it as received through an unbroken succession, the Blessed Lord said: “I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvān, the Sun; Vivasvān taught it to Manu, his son; and Manu declared it to Ikṣvāku, his son.” Its fruit is imperishable, and therefore the yoga is called imperishable.
word_for_word: for the purpose of discriminating the meaning of “That” and “Thou”
the means of karma-yoga and the means of knowledge-yoga

2.translation: Thus the royal sages and other kings who were also sages, beginning with Nimi, learned this yoga as it was taught through the succession beginning with Ikṣvāku and his descendants. Śrīdhara explains the cause of the present age’s ignorance: “O scorcher of foes, that yoga has been lost in this world through the power of time; its succession has been severed.”
word_for_word: those kings who were also sages
taught by their sons and descendants
the cause of the present people’s ignorance

3.translation: That same ancient yoga, now that its succession has been broken, has been spoken by Me to you today. Śrīdhara explains that it is being given to Arjuna because he is My devotee and friend; it is not spoken to just anyone, for this is the highest secret.
word_for_word: today, when the succession has been broken
has again been spoken by Me to you
it is not spoken by Me to another

4.translation: Arjuna, seeing an apparent impossibility in teaching the yoga to Vivasvān, said: “Your birth was later and Vivasvān’s birth was earlier; therefore, how am I to understand that You taught this yoga at the beginning?”
word_for_word: seeing the impossibility of the Lord’s teaching the yoga to Vivasvān
your birth was later / more recent
you taught the yoga at the beginning

5.translation: The Blessed Lord said: “Many births of Mine have passed, and yours also, O Arjuna. I know all of them because My power of knowledge is never lost; but you do not know them because you are covered by ignorance.”
word_for_word: because the power of knowledge is not lost
because of being covered by ignorance

6.translation: “Although unborn, although of imperishable nature, and although the Lord of beings, I still manifest through My own māyā, having taken My own pure-sattva nature as My basis. I descend by My own will in a pure and exalted sattvic form.” Śrīdhara gives this answer to the question of how the Lord, free from merit and demerit and independent of karma, can take birth like an ordinary living being.
word_for_word: but, for one without a beginning, how can there be birth
and how can one who is indestructible be born again
for you, who are the Lord

with a form of pure and exalted sattva

7.translation: Śrīdhara answers the question of when the Lord manifests: “Whenever there is a decline of dharma, O Bhārata, and a rise of adharma, at that time I manifest Myself.” Here decline means the loss of dharma, and rise means the predominance of adharma.

8.translation: “For the protection of the virtuous, who follow their own dharma; for the destruction of the harmful, who perform evil actions; and for establishing dharma, I manifest in every age, at each such time.” Establishing dharma means making it firm through protecting the virtuous and destroying the harmful. Śrīdhara says that the Lord’s destruction of the harmful should not be regarded as cruelty, just as a mother is not unmerciful when disciplining a child.
word_for_word: for the protection of the virtuous
of those who follow their own dharma
and for the destruction of the harmful
for the purpose of establishing dharma

9.translation: “Whoever knows in truth that My birth is self-willed and that My action, in the form of preserving dharma, is divine and beyond the ordinary world, leaves behind bodily identification at death, is not reborn, and reaches Me, O Arjuna.” Śrīdhara adds that the Lord’s manifestation and action are undertaken for the benefit of others.
word_for_word: of the Lord’s birth and action
having the form of preserving dharma
for the benefit of others alone
having abandoned identification with the body

10.translation: Śrīdhara explains how knowing the Lord’s birth and action leads to attaining Him. Knowing that the Lord, through incarnations of pure sattva, protects dharma and is supremely compassionate, many have become free from attachment, fear, and anger. With their minds absorbed in Him and taking refuge in Him alone, they were purified by knowledge and austerity: Self-knowledge received by His grace, together with the dharma that matures that austerity. Having removed ignorance and its effects, they attained His state, union with Him. This is not a path that began only in the present.
word_for_word: how through knowledge of birth and action
free from attachment, fear, and anger
absorbed in Me / made of Me

na tu adhunā eva pravṛttaḥ ayam mat-bhakti-mārgaḥ
this path of devotion to Me did not begin only now

11.translation: If there were partiality in the Lord, He would give His own state only to those who take refuge in Him, not to those who approach with desires. Śrīdhara answers: “In whatever way people worship Me—with desire or without desire—I bless them in that very way, granting the result they seek. Do not think that I neglect those who, leaving Me aside, worship only Indra and the other gods; in every way they follow My path, because I alone am to be worshiped even in the form of Indra and the others.”

12.translation: Those who desire the accomplishment—the fruit—of actions generally worship the gods such as Indra in this human world, rather than worshiping Me directly. The fruit born of action comes quickly, whereas the fruit of knowledge, liberation, is not quickly obtained because knowledge is difficult to attain.
word_for_word: for the sake of liberation alone
why do not all worship You
worship the gods beginning with Indra
because knowledge is difficult to attain
